caveats: The brain's step runs against a 150 ms deadline (0.85 of the 176 ms tick) and the encoder drive goes stale on any tick it overruns. The cost of a step is edges touched = N x firing rate x degree, so a hotter condition costs more; overrun is then a STEP function of that cost against the deadline, so conditions clustered near it can show wildly different overrun fractions for a few ms of difference. Measured this run (mean_ms_per_tick / overrun_fraction): real 81.2 ms / 0.0005, lesion:DNp01 61.2 ms / 0, lesion:DNa02 86.8 ms / 0, lesion:optic 69.9 ms / 0, ablate-network 53.2 ms / 0, shuffle 134.0 ms / 0.0695. Staleness IS a live confound on any contrast involving shuffle (0.0695): those conditions ran stale drive on that fraction of their ticks, and the conditions they are measured against did not do so to the same degree.

The decoded drive sits near 0.10 with a steering differential of about +/-0.1 rad, so directed movement is slow and the steering metrics (distance, tortuosity) are correspondingly noisy. Kills were not zero in every condition this run: real 10.2/hr, lesion:DNa02 10.2/hr
shuffle_verdict: SHUFFLE DEGRADED vs real: the connectome's specific wiring does work beyond its degree sequence and transmitter signs.
